This paired fixture is an artificial repository-context stress evaluation, not evidence of real large-project performance. Both cases specify the same task and hidden tests. The expanded case adds only independent distractor modules under stress_pkg/distractors/; these are explicitly artificial, unrelated to the task, and should remain untouched.

Fix the existing target module stress_pkg/z_intervals.py. Keep its public API merge_intervals(intervals: Iterable[tuple[int, int]]) -> list[tuple[int, int]]. Do not add task-count or planning assumptions.

Dependency contract: stress_pkg/interval_policy.py exports validate_interval(raw: object) -> tuple[int, int]. It accepts only an exact tuple of length two whose endpoints have exact type int (bool is invalid) and whose start is <= end. Signed endpoints are valid. Any invalid value raises ValueError("invalid interval"). It returns the same endpoint pair. The target must call this validator exactly once for every supplied interval, including empty intervals, and propagate its error.

Intervals denote half-open ranges [start, end). Consume the iterable once; it may be a generator. Ignore empty intervals after validation. Return a new list of sorted, non-empty, maximal ranges whose union equals the union of the input. Merge intervals that overlap or touch at a boundary; duplicate intervals have no extra effect. Preserve negative endpoints. Empty input returns []. Do not mutate the input or add another dependency.

Existing stress_pkg/test_intervals.py tests are green against the seed and must keep passing. The target file is intentionally sorted after the distractor module paths so the functional task is on an existing late-path module. No filesystem, network, database, third-party packages, or external state.
